newsitem.title: UK: European shares lag Wall St, dollar below highs.
newsitem.headline: European shares lag Wall St, dollar below highs.

text.p: European shares rose on Monday, taking their cue from Friday's rebound on Wall Street, but failed to hold on to part of their gains despite a new surge on the New York market when it reopened.
Nagging fears of higher interest rates and uncertainty on the outlook for Wall Street, the world's biggest stock market, further down the road helped trim gains by mid-afternoon.
"It's been a cautious day and we've not really seen any real demand," one London share trader said.
"One would have expected a better start to what is effectively the first trading day of the new year," a senior London dealer said. "People are wary about the interest rate picture."
The Dow Jones industrial average was up around 37 points at 6,581 in the first hour of New York trading on Monday after jumping 101.60 points to 6,544.09 on Friday.

On the bullion market, gold, which has been shunned by investors as stock markets hit record levels and low inflation detracted from its status as a "safe haven", slipped further to its lowest fix since October 7, 1993.
The gold price dropped late last week as New York-based investment funds sold. "We've seen continued fund selling last week," one bullion dealer said. "No one wants to touch it."

The dollar, meanwhile, was knocked off its strongest level against the yen since March 1993 after Vice Finance Minister Tadashi Ogawa said Japan would "continue to deal appropriately" with extreme currency market movements.

Excessive weakness or strength in the yen was not good for the Japanese economy, he said. The dollar, which flirted with 117 yen in Asian trading, then hit a 115.40 low in European business, below late rates last week.
"Japanese officials will get increasingly edgy about seeing yen weakness and I think official disapproval of such a move will be enough to limit it," said Standard Chartered's Tim Fox.
But analysts said negative perceptions of the Japanese economy and low interest rates there still prompted concern over an outflow of funds and should continue to bolster the dollar.
Tokyo markets made a shaky start to the new year on Monday as the yen slid to its lowest level against the dollar in almost four years, dragging stocks and bonds down in its wake.
The 225-share Nikkei average fell by as much as 150 points before reviving to close at 19,446.00, up 84.65 points.
Against the mark, the U.S. currency slipped from a high in Asian trading of 1.5714 but, at around 1.5630 marks, it was still above Friday's late European levels.

The pound sterling hit its highest level against the mark in more than four years before subsiding. It stood at 2.6325 marks, compared with an early high of 2.6615, its peak since crashing out of the European exchange rate mechanism in September 1992.
On the London stock market, Europe's busiest, shares started firmer after Wall Street's revival but fear of higher U.S. and British interest rates held them back.

"After the Dow's 100-point jump last Friday, a mark-up in London was inevitable but some players are worried about the Dow's volatility," a London dealer said. "The market knows the Dow could just as easily drop 100 points in a day, especially if we get any data which hints at higher rates.
In Frankfurt, shares were firmer, aided by the stronger dollar -- good news for German exporters -- and the rebound in New York. But bourse floor trade closed below the day's highs.

French shares also began the week higher, buoyed by Wall Street's gains and the dollar's performance. Hopes of French interest rate cuts lived on, particularly after changes in the Bank of France monetary policy council.

This week the main focus for markets will be U.S. jobs figures on Friday. If non-farm payroll statistics are stronger than forecast, raising fears of an overheating economy and higher inflation, jitters over higher rates could send stock and bond markets lower on both sides of the Atlantic, dealers said.
The dollar is also highly sensitive to moves in U.S. stock and bond markets, they noted.
German November manufacturing orders, December unemployment and December cost of living numbers are also due in coming days.
CURRENCIES AT 1530 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.5630 marks and 115.50 yen, compared with 1.5580 and 116.33 in late business on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1530 GMT
London's FTSE 100 index was up 10.0 points to 4,099.5.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt ended floor trade 22.04 points higher at 2,881.32 and changed little in later electronic trading. In Paris the CAC-40 index was up 17.69 at 2,300.45.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $358.50 an ounce in the afternoon, down from a morning fix of $359.25 and Friday's London close of $362.15. Silver was down just one cent at $4.68.
